## Problem 1
```{r problem 1}
library(tidyverse)
same_birthday = function(n) {
  birthday_vector = sample(1:365, size = n, replace = TRUE)
  n_distinct(birthday_vector) < n
}
same_birthday(30)

sim_results = expand_grid(
  range = 2:50,
  iter = 1:10000
) |>
  mutate(repeated = map_lgl(range, same_birthday)) |>
  group_by(range) |>
  summarize(
    probability = mean(repeated)
  )

sim_plot = sim_results |>
  ggplot(aes(x = range, y = probability)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    title = "Probability of a Shared Birthday",
    x = "Group size",
    y = "Estimated probability"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

sim_plot
```
As the group size increases, the probability that at least two people share a birthday also increases. The probability is about 50% for a group of 23 people and about 97% for a group of 50 people. This shows that shared birthdays are common even in groups much smaller than 365 people.
